_comment: Pitch boundaries, one per camera, drawn in the editor at /roi.
Points are [x, y] as fractions of the frame (0-1), so a resolution change does
not invalidate them. Everything outside the outline is filled before the frame
Committed on purpose: a boundary is geometry, not a credential, and re-drawing
one by hand after a clone is setup nobody repeats identically.
`_aliases` maps a camera id as production names it (venue/camera, or the worker's
file0/file1 under a recording key) onto the key a boundary is stored under; see
_aliases_comment: A36 (2026-09-19). Production knows venue_01's cameras as camera_A / camera_B
(configs/cameras.json, slots_schedule.json); the derived store knows them per
recording as slot_<date>_<time>_camA / camB. db/seed.py PHYSICAL_CAMERA says which
recording view is which physical camera. These point each production id at the
daytime recording's outline of that physical camera; confirm or redraw at /roi.
The worker's file0/file1 keys need no alias - roi.resolve maps them per recording.
_venue_01_comment: venue_01 has TWO physical cameras and FOUR slot-camera names, and until 2026-09-21 it
had four different derived boundaries - three of which disagreed with each other about
the same view. db/seed.PHYSICAL_CAMERA is the mapping: slot_20260711_1000_camA and
slot_20260712_2030_camB are both camera_A; slot_20260711_1000_camB and
The derived ones came from scripts/derive_roi.py - the convex hull of the largest green
region in a median frame - and on floodlit night footage that finds only the bright
foreground. slot_20260712_2030_camB's derived outline covered the lower-left of the frame
and EXCLUDED the goalmouth and the right-hand third, so a frame with eleven players in it
counted zero inside the boundary and the rule answered EMPTY at confidence 1.00. That
camera is 516 frames, the largest single group in the corpus.
These two are drawn by hand from the day frames of each physical camera, where the far
touchline is visible, and checked against the night frames of the same camera. They follow
the turf rather than the painted lines, because a player standing on the touchline is on
the pitch. camera_B's stops at x=0.95 to exclude the blue railings and the car park beyond
them; the old derived outline reached y=0.18 and took in the playground and the street.
